Q: How to bin a 2D array in numpy? A:

I find it most useful to use numpy.searchsorted() for this, based on this post for binning 1D arrays. When I have an 2D array dta with dta.shape = (x,y) for some x, y bigger than 1, we can bin the array into bins using this aproach:

import numpy as np

start = 0     # lower bin boundary
stop = 1      # upper bin boundary
num_bins = 10 # number of individual bins

# vector of bins
bins_spacing = np.linspace(start = start, stop = stop, num = num_bins + 1)

# assign each element in dta the index corresponding to its bin index
bin_indecies = np.searchsorted(a=bins_spacing, v = dta, side='left')

# create a dict to hold your data
bins = {}

# loop over the bins
for i in range(num_bins):
    bins.update({str(i): dta[np.where(bin_indecies[:, 0] == i, True, False), :]})

# compute number of elements in each bin
nums = [len(bins[str(i)]) for i in range(len(bins))]

# compute the mean for each bin
means = [np.mean(bins[str(i)][:, 0]) for i in range(len(bins))]

# compute the std for each bin
stds = [np.std(bins[str(i)][:, 0]) for i in range(len(bins))]

This you can also use to compute any other aspect of your bins. I hope this answer is still helpful even though it may be clear by now how to do this...

Q: SUM returns `NULL` instead of 0 when all values are `NULL` in Apache IoTDB A:

Using CASE expression:

SELECT product_id, 
    CASE SUM(sales_amount) IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE SUM(sales_amount) END AS total 
FROM product_sales 
GROUP BY product_id;
